Daily Digest Friday, June 26, 2026

Zeta + Palantir Build Agentic Stack, Forrester Warns on AI-for-Efficiency Trap, Agentforce Commerce Goes GA

Zeta + Palantir build agentic marketing infrastructure. Forrester warns agencies are trading creativity for cost savings. Salesforce launches AI commerce agents.

  1. 1

    Zeta + Palantir Partner on Agentic Marketing Infrastructure

    Zeta Global will rearchitect its Data Cloud on Palantir Foundry, combining Zeta's Athena AI engine with Palantir's data governance and ontology layer. The goal: real-time marketing decisions powered by governed operational data. Zeta CEO David Steinberg says the deal could generate $100M+ annually. This is the kind of enterprise infrastructure play that makes agentic marketing actually work at scale.

    Read on MarTech ↗
  2. 2

    Forrester: 90% of Agencies Use AI — But It's Undermining Effectiveness

    Released at Cannes Lions with the 4As, Forrester's State of AI Inside US Marketing Agencies report delivers a warning: nine in ten agencies now use genAI, half use agentic AI — but the industry is "systematically trading creativity for cost savings." Top use cases? Summarizing docs (74%) and competitive research (70%). The question CMOs should ask their agencies: where are the efficiency gains being reinvested? If the answer is margin, the brand is being hollowed out.

    Read on Agile Brand Guide ↗
  3. 3

    Salesforce Agentforce Commerce Goes GA with Three AI Agents

    Salesforce dropped its biggest Agentforce Commerce release yet: Shopper Agent, Buyer Agent, and Merchant Agent all go generally available, with native integration into ChatGPT, Google Search AI Mode, and Gemini coming this summer. The numbers: AI influenced 20% of global online sales ($262B) last holiday season, and AI-referred traffic converts at 8x the rate of social. Salesforce EVP Nitin Mangtani: "The brands that win will have their Shopper Agent live for the 2026 shopping season."

    Read on Agile Brand Guide ↗
  4. 4

    MoEngage Acquires Aampe: A Different Agentic Bet

    MoEngage acquires Aampe to bring 1:1 agentic decisioning to B2C marketing — one AI agent per individual customer, running 200 billion decisions per week. This is architecturally different from Salesforce's broader platform approach: narrower, deeper, and operationally proven. The trade-off: less platform lock-in, more data infrastructure investment. CMOs need to decide which problem they're actually solving before picking a path.

    Read on Agile Brand Guide ↗
  5. 5

    Adobe GenStudio Ships Brand-Aware Content Creation at Cannes

    Adobe GenStudio updated its enterprise product suite with AI that remembers corporate voice guidelines, colors, logos, and strategic priorities across design sessions. The system now manages end-to-end content creation, compliance reviews, and campaign analytics. Meanwhile, ActiveCampaign's Active Intelligence 2.8 takes a similar approach for email sequences. The pattern: enterprise AI is moving from "generate anything" to "generate within our brand rails." Read this one: The Agile Brand Guide's analysis of yesterday's Cannes news — particularly the three signals on the efficiency-vs-effectiveness trap, the agentic AI architecture split, and why data readiness is the real bottleneck. Most organizations aren't blocked by AI capability. They're blocked by data infrastructure that can't support the tools they want to deploy.
